note: W1-LIBRARY round 3. The short tail of a written culture of arms: what gets cut into a lintel, chanted at a drill, nailed to a market post, written on the back of a challenge, argued about in a stores book, folded into a helmet, and sung by children who do not know they are being drilled. None is under 150 words, because the corpus's short tail was already nearly twice Morrowind's; these sit in the 180-450 band the measured distribution is thin at. The two endings of the counting rhyme disagree and both towns are sure theirs is older, and the serjeant's remark is the only thing in the library that says which drill is right.

books.title: Inscription Over the Gate of the Depot at Thorn
books.author: cut by an unknown hand; the second and third lines are in a different chisel and are later
books.unreliability: Three hands over an unknown span, each answering the last, on a lintel nobody has authority to correct. The Cohort walks under all three every morning and the depot book records the cutting of none of them.
books.text:
*(Cut into the stone lintel over the gate of the Ninth Cohort's depot at Thorn. Three hands. The first is deep and even and Imperial; the second is shallower and the letters are wider apart; the third is scratched rather than cut and is at the very edge of the stone where a person standing on the wall-walk could reach down.)*

BY THE ORDER OF THE PROVINCIAL OFFICE
THIS STATION IS SET HERE FOR THE PEACE OF THE PROVINCE
AND THE HONOUR OF THE NINTH

*(second hand, below:)*

AND FOR THE SALT

*(third hand, at the edge, small:)*

we cut the stone and we hauled it and we set it
and no officer asked us what to put on it
so this

*(A note in the depot book, in the quartermaster-clerk's hand, undated:)* The Office has twice written asking under whose authority the second and third lines were cut and by whom, and I have twice answered that the depot has no record. That is true. What the depot also has no record of is the cutting of the first line, the setting of the lintel, the building of the gate, or the raising of the wall, the depot book beginning in 3E 402 and the station being older than that by a good deal. I have not put the second half of that answer in either letter.

The serjeant-instructor has asked me to record that the men touch the third line going out and not coming in. He does not know when this began. He stopped asking, and he touches it himself.

books.title: Handbill: The Ninth Cohort Takes Auxiliaries at Gideon, Archon and Stormhold
books.author: Provincial Office at Gideon, printed by the hundred and nailed at every chartered market
books.unreliability: Every figure on it is accurate and every figure on it is the gross. The stoppages are on the reverse in the smallest type the press at Gideon owns, and the burial fund's terms are not on the bill at all.
books.wrong_on_purpose: Advertises the burial fund as repayable at twenty years without stating that the term does not run on a second engagement, which is where most auxiliaries who reach twenty years are.
books.text:
**THE NINTH COHORT**
**TAKES AUXILIARIES**

At the depot gate, Gideon. At the customs house, Archon. At the water stair, Stormhold.
Any day but the water-call.

**WHO MAY COME.** Any person of this province of 16 years or over who can walk 12 miles and carry a load. No test of letters. No fee. No sponsor required and none accepted.

**WHAT YOU ARE PAID.** Six drakes the month from the day you are taken. Twelve as a file-leader. Twenty as a decurion, and the Ninth has had 3 Argonian decurions and would like more.

**WHAT YOU ARE GIVEN.** A sword of the marsh pattern. Boots twice a year. Two meals every day of your service, in every season, whether the season has given anything or not.

**WHAT YOU MAY KEEP.** Your own name. Your own weapon if you bring one and it is sound. Your own household — an auxiliary of this Cohort may not be posted more than 4 days from the landing he was taken at, by standing order, and the order has been kept for 60 years.

**THE BURIAL FUND.** One drake the month is stopped and returned to you entire at 20 years' service.

**WHAT IT IS NOT.** It is not a lease. It is not signed before the Assize. There is no term and no bond, and an auxiliary of this Cohort may take his discharge at any water-call by asking the serjeant of his depot for it, and no serjeant may refuse.

Bring nothing. Ask at the gate for the serjeant-instructor.

*Long live the Emperor Uriel Septim VII.*

*(On the reverse, in type a third the size:)* Stoppages: 2 drakes the month for kit and replacement; 1 drake the month for the burial fund; laundry, 4 drakes the year; loss or damage to issued kit at the quartermaster's valuation, which is final. Rates given are before stoppages. Discharge at a water-call is subject to the completion of the current engagement.

books.title: Rack Tally, Depot at Thorn, Quarterly, With the Quartermaster's Note and Two Others
books.author: kept by the quartermaster-clerk at Thorn; the second and third hands are not identified in the book
books.unreliability: A count that does not agree with itself twice running, in a document whose entire purpose is to agree with itself. Nobody in it is dishonest. The explanation offered in the third hand is almost certainly correct and would end the quartermaster's career.
books.text:
*(A leaf from the stores book of the depot at Thorn. Four quarters, one under the other. Two later hands.)*

**Sun's Height.** Racked and counted by me, alone, against the book.

Swords, marsh pattern .... 44 (book 44)
Swords, garrison ......... 12 (book 12)
Bills .................... 22 (book 22)
Axes, splitter ........... 0 (book 0)
Shields, kite ............ 38 (book 38)
Poles .................... 61 (book 60)

*Pole surplus of 1. Auxiliaries cut their own and leave them. Entered and not pursued.*

**Frostfall.** Racked and counted by me and by the serjeant-instructor, together.

Swords, marsh pattern .... 41 (book 44)
Swords, garrison ......... 12 (book 12)
Bills .................... 22 (book 22)
Axes, splitter ........... 0 (book 0)
Shields, kite ............ 38 (book 38)
Poles .................... 66 (book 60)

*Short 3 marsh pattern. Reported. No explanation offered by any file. Nothing forced, nothing broken, gate log clean.*

**Sun's Dawn.** Racked and counted by me, alone.

Swords, marsh pattern .... 44 (book 41)
Poles .................... 59 (book 66)

*Over by 3, the exact number short at Frostfall. All 3 in the rack, in the right places, and 2 of them are not the ones that were taken. I have not entered this as a correction because I do not know what to correct.*

*(second hand, in the margin, small:)*
Which quarter did the lease convoys run in? Ask.

*(third hand, pencil, at the foot of the leaf, and it has been rubbed and written again:)*
Both. That's the point. They go out with the convoy and they come back with the convoy, and the count is only ever wrong at the quarter in between.

No one's stealing anything. Someone is borrowing 3 swords, twice a year, for about 9 weeks, and putting swords back.

Not the same swords.

books.title: The Line, a Counting Rhyme, As Children Sing It at Gideon and at Archon
books.author: traditional; the Archon version differs at the fourth line and at the end, and the difference is given below
books.unreliability: A children's rhyme that is a drill, and the adults who taught it to the children have all forgotten that. The two endings are irreconcilable and both towns are certain theirs is the old one.
books.text:
*(A skipping and clapping rhyme. The children stand in a row with linked arms and one child goes along the row trying to get through. Sung at Gideon; the Archon version is below.)*

Shoulder, shoulder, rim on rim,
who's the one they're letting in?
Not the front and not the back,
mind the middle, mind the crack.

One for the sword and one for the hook,
one for the lad who's writing the book,
one for the wall and one for the door,
one for the one who isn't there any more.

Lock, lock, nothing gets by.
Lock, lock, don't you cry.
Lock, lock, hold your ground!
And down goes the little one, down goes the little one,
down goes the little one, and the row does not turn round.

*(At the last line the row breaks and the smallest child is pulled down, and the row closes over where they were, and the game begins again with the same child, who must lie still until it does.)*

---

*At Archon the fourth line is sung "mind the middle, mind your back," and the last three lines are:*

Lock, lock, hold your ground!
And up comes the little one, up comes the little one,
up comes the little one, and the whole row turns round.

*(At Archon the row lifts the smallest child over their heads and passes them along it to the end, and the child who was trying to get through has to start again.)*

*A serjeant of the Ninth who was quartered at both towns is said to have remarked that the Gideon children were being taught the instruction and the Archon children were being taught the thing that actually works, and to have been told to keep his voice down.*
